change.title: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader
change.diff:
--- /dev/null
+++ b/db/migrations/0042_reader_shard_grants.sql
@@ -0,0 +1,3 @@
+-- Make the reader's access to shard databases explicit so per-principal
+-- query limits and audit logging apply to it.
+GRANT SELECT ON r0.* TO svc_bundle_reader;

verdict.headline: Explicit shard grants for svc_bundle_reader are safe: bundle size doubles but worker-runtime handles it
verdict.cause: The change adds GRANT SELECT ON r0.* to svc_bundle_reader, which causes the bundle-builder to read both default.bundle_fields (99 rows) and r0.bundle_fields (99 rows), doubling the bundle from 99 to 198 entries (3118→6187 bytes). However, worker-runtime exits with code 0 in both baseline and candidate, showing the increased bundle size does not violate any runtime limits.
tested: x-311801189aae44f9: baseline · workload default → all assertions passed
x-ede6ef4efe6e4749: candidate · workload default → all assertions passed
limitations: Could not verify exact value of worker-runtime.max_entries setting; experiments showed runtime handles the doubled bundle size without exit code change
Baseline and candidate both passed under every tested workload.

experiments.rationale: Compare baseline (without explicit r0 grant) to establish normal operation metrics
Compare candidate (with explicit r0.* grant) to see if bundle output changes

hypotheses.claim: The explicit grant on r0.* will cause the bundle-builder's query to return additional rows or different column metadata from r0.bundle_fields compared to default.bundle_fields, changing the bundle.json artifact and potentially exceeding worker-runtime.max_entries
hypotheses.mechanism: The bundle-builder query SELECT name, type FROM system.columns WHERE table = 'bundle_fields' ORDER BY name will now include rows from r0.bundle_fields in addition to default.bundle_fields. If r0.bundle_fields has different column count or content, the bundle.json will have more entries, potentially exceeding worker-runtime.max_entries and causing startup failure.
